REDLINE ANALYSIS MEMORANDUM
Executive Employment Agreement — Counterparty Markup Review

TO:		Client / Engagement Partner
FROM:		Employment & Labor Practice
DATE:		[Engagement Date]
RE:		Analyze Counterparty Markup of Executive Employment Agreement — Advisory Memorandum
MATTER:	Matter File 12 — Employment Labor
OUTPUT:	redline-analysis-memorandum.docx

================================================================================
I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
================================================================================

This memorandum reviews the counterparty’s redline of the Company’s form Executive Employment Agreement against the Company draft and applicable employment-labor guidance, market practice for senior executive arrangements, and firm precedent. The analysis identifies material deviations, assesses risk and leverage, and recommends accept / reject / counter positions with proposed fallback language.

Overall assessment. The counterparty markup systematically shifts economics, termination economics, restrictive-covenant scope, and dispute posture in favor of the executive. Several edits are within market for C-suite hires and can be accepted or lightly revised. A smaller set of edits — particularly around “Good Reason” triggers, equity acceleration on termination without Cause, post-termination non-compete duration and geographic scope, clawback carve-outs, and perpetual or overbroad indemnification/advancement — are outside Company precedent and should be rejected or tightly cabined.

Priority issues (in order of commercial significance):

1. Definition of “Cause” and “Good Reason” (termination economics and walk-away rights).
2. Severance multiple, COBRA subsidy, and bonus treatment on involuntary termination / resignation for Good Reason.
3. Equity treatment (time-based vs. performance awards; single- vs. double-trigger acceleration).
4. Restrictive covenants (non-compete, non-solicit, non-disparagement, confidentiality duration and scope).
5. Clawback, recoupment, and compliance with Company policies / Dodd-Frank / exchange listing rules.
6. Indemnification, D&O coverage, and advancement of expenses.
7. Dispute resolution (arbitration, governing law, venue, fee-shifting).
8. At-will / term structure, renewal, and notice mechanics.

Recommendation posture. Engage constructively on market-standard executive protections; hold firm on Cause definition, double-trigger equity, clawback alignment, and enforceable but reasonable restrictive covenants. Do not accept open-ended Good Reason constructs or unilateral amendment rights that effectively convert the arrangement into a fixed-term guaranteed package without corresponding Company protections.

================================================================================
II. SCOPE, MATERIALS, AND METHOD
================================================================================

A. Engagement instruction. Review the counterparty’s redline of the attached employment agreement against the company draft and referenced guidance materials, and prepare a comprehensive advisory memo (this deliverable).

B. Operative materials (Matter File 12).
   - Company draft Executive Employment Agreement (baseline).
   - Counterparty redline / markup of the Executive Employment Agreement.
   - Referenced guidance materials and firm employment-labor precedent.
   - Matter file framing: representations and warranties, covenants, conditions, indemnification, and termination provisions negotiated between the parties; open issues flagged for analysis against firm precedent and market practice.

C. Method. For each material provision we: (1) restate Company draft position; (2) describe counterparty edit; (3) assess deviation vs. market and Company precedent; (4) assign risk rating (Low / Moderate / High / Critical); (5) recommend Accept / Accept with revision / Counter / Reject; and (6) supply proposed counter language or fallback where useful.

D. Assumptions. Analysis assumes a U.S. private or public company senior executive hire (CEO / President / C-suite or equivalent), at-will or initial fixed term with automatic renewal, cash + target bonus + equity package, and standard confidentiality / IP assignment. Jurisdiction-specific enforceability of non-competes (e.g., California, Colorado, Illinois, New York, FTC/state developments) must be confirmed against the executive’s work location and governing law before signature. This memorandum is advisory within the simulated engagement and is not a substitute for jurisdiction-specific enforceability opinions.

================================================================================
III. ISSUE-BY-ISSUE REDLINE ANALYSIS
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. PARTIES, POSITION, DUTIES, AND REPORTING
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Company draft: Executive employed in stated title, reporting to Board / CEO as applicable, full-time devotion, duties consistent with position, permitted outside activities only with prior written consent and subject to conflict rules.

Counterparty markup (typical pattern): Broadens “duties consistent with position” to duties “customarily associated with” the title at peer companies; adds express right to serve on outside boards (often up to a stated number) and engage in charitable/civic activities without consent; softens full-time devotion; may insert “principal” place of work with remote/hybrid flexibility and relocation consent rights.

Assessment: Outside board service and civic activity are market for senior executives if capped (e.g., one for-profit board, unlimited non-profit subject to conflict and time), pre-cleared, and subordinate to Company duties. Uncapped outside boards and unilateral remote/relocation rights are not.

Risk: Moderate.

Recommendation: ACCEPT WITH REVISION.
- Cap outside for-profit boards (suggest: one, with prior Board consent not to be unreasonably withheld).
- Require advance notice of non-profit roles; preserve conflict and time-commitment override.
- Keep reporting line and material duty changes tied to Good Reason only if demotion-level (see §3).
- Place of performance: permit remote/hybrid consistent with Company policy; relocation outside a stated radius (e.g., 35–50 miles) only by mutual written agreement, with Good Reason if Company mandates relocation beyond that radius without consent.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. TERM; AT-WILL; RENEWAL; NOTICE
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Company draft: Employment at-will, or initial term (e.g., three years) with automatic one-year renewals unless either party gives advance notice (e.g., 90 days); survival of restrictive covenants, IP, and indemnification.

Counterparty markup: Often converts to hard fixed term with Company-only non-renewal treated as termination without Cause; lengthens notice Company must give; may require Company to pay out remaining term on non-renewal.

Assessment: Treating Company non-renewal as without-Cause termination is a significant economic shift and is sometimes granted for CEO-level hires, rarely below that without offsetting concessions. Evergreen with mutual notice is preferable to hard term payout.

Risk: High (if non-renewal = without Cause with full severance).

Recommendation: COUNTER.
- Prefer at-will with severance protections on without-Cause / Good Reason termination (cleaner than term payout).
- If fixed term retained: automatic renewal; either-party non-renewal on ≥90 days’ notice; Company non-renewal may trigger a reduced severance (e.g., 50–100% of without-Cause package) only for CEO and only if equity is not also single-trigger accelerated.
- Reject remaining-term salary guarantee stacked on top of full severance.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. “CAUSE” DEFINITION
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Company draft (illustrative baseline): Cause includes (i) material breach of agreement or policy after notice and cure (where curable); (ii) willful failure to perform material duties after notice/cure; (iii) fraud, embezzlement, or willful misconduct; (iv) conviction or plea regarding felony or crime of moral turpitude; (v) material violation of restrictive covenants or fiduciary duties; (vi) willful conduct materially harming the Company.

Counterparty markup: Inserts “willful and material” qualifiers broadly; adds opportunity to cure almost all prongs (including fraud); requires Board supermajority finding after opportunity to be heard with counsel; excludes good-faith actions taken in believed best interests of Company; narrows crimes to those directly related to employment; deletes policy-violation prong or limits to written policies provided in advance.

Assessment: Cure rights for performance/breach prongs and a hearing opportunity are market for executives. Cure for fraud/embezzlement, supermajority Board votes, and deletion of policy/fiduciary prongs are executive-favorable beyond typical mid-market precedent and erode Company control.

Risk: Critical.

Recommendation: REJECT key dilutions; ACCEPT limited process rights.
- Retain fraud, embezzlement, felony/crime involving dishonesty or moral turpitude, and willful misconduct without cure.
- Permit 15–30 day cure only for curable material breach and failure-to-perform prongs.
- Board determination in good faith after notice and opportunity to be heard is acceptable; reject supermajority or independent-director-only requirements unless public-company governance demands it.
- Keep material violation of written Company policies (provided or reasonably available) and restrictive covenants as Cause.
- Proposed formulation note: define “willful” as acting in bad faith or without reasonable belief that conduct was in Company’s best interests (Caremark/Disney-style), not mere negligence.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. “GOOD REASON” DEFINITION
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Company draft: Narrow Good Reason — material diminution in title, duties, or reporting; material reduction in base salary (other than across-the-board ≤10%); material breach by Company — each with notice and 30-day cure, and resignation within a short window after cure period.

Counterparty markup: Expands to include: any change in duties or reporting even if not material; reduction in target bonus or equity opportunity; relocation beyond a short distance; failure to nominate to Board; change in control itself (single-trigger walk right); adverse change in benefit plans; requirement to travel more than a stated amount; successor’s failure to assume.

Assessment: Expansive Good Reason is the primary leakage point for severance and equity acceleration. Single-trigger CIC Good Reason and non-material duty changes are particularly problematic.

Risk: Critical.

Recommendation: COUNTER / REJECT overbreadth.
- Accept: material diminution in position, authority, duties, or base salary; material Company breach; relocation of principal workplace beyond 50 miles (if on-site role).
- Reject or tightly limit: reduction in target bonus/equity solely due to Board recalibration consistent with peer roles; pure CIC without adverse employment impact; travel increases; benefit plan changes applicable to senior executives generally.
- Process: executive written notice within 60 days of knowledge of event; 30-day Company cure; resignation effective within 30–60 days after cure expiry. Failure to follow process = waiver.
- Do not accept Good Reason that can be asserted based on subjective dissatisfaction with strategy or Board direction.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. COMPENSATION: BASE, BONUS, EQUITY ELIGIBILITY
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Company draft: Stated base salary (reviewable, not reducible except as in Good Reason); target annual bonus as % of base, based on performance goals set by Board/Comp Committee; eligibility for equity under Company plan subject to separate award agreements; benefits on same basis as peer executives; expense reimbursement per policy.

Counterparty markup: Base “not less than” current with mandatory annual COLA or only-upward reviews; guaranteed bonus (or minimum payout floor); target bonus deemed earned if employed on last day of year regardless of performance; signing bonus with weak clawback; equity grant size and vesting schedule hardwired into employment agreement rather than award agreements; “best-of” benefits.

Assessment: Guaranteed or formula-deemed bonuses undermine pay-for-performance and Comp Committee discretion. Hardwiring equity terms into the employment agreement creates amendment friction and plan-administration conflict.

Risk: High (bonus guarantees / equity hardwire); Moderate (salary floor language).

Recommendation: COUNTER.
- Base: “initial” base, reviewed at least annually; no obligation to increase; reductions only per Good Reason construct.
- Bonus: target opportunity only; actual payout per plan goals and Comp Committee certification; proration on termination only as specified in severance section; reject “deemed earned” language.
- Signing bonus: acceptable with clawback if executive resigns without Good Reason or is terminated for Cause within 12–24 months.
- Equity: employment agreement states eligibility and, if needed, initial grant guidelines; specific share counts, vesting, and acceleration live in award agreements and plan documents, which control in conflict.
- Benefits: participation on terms applicable to similarly situated executives; Company retains right to amend plans prospectively on a non-discriminatory basis.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. SEVERANCE AND TERMINATION ECONOMICS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Company draft (illustrative): On termination without Cause or resignation for Good Reason: (i) accrued obligations; (ii) cash severance equal to [1.0x–1.5x] base (CEO often 1.5x–2.0x); (iii) COBRA subsidy for severance period; (iv) pro-rata bonus based on actual performance; (v) limited equity treatment per award agreements. Conditioned on timely release and compliance with restrictive covenants. Death/disability: accrued + pro-rata bonus + equity per plan. For Cause / without Good Reason: accrued only.

Counterparty markup: Increases multiple (e.g., to 2x–3x base+bonus); includes target (not actual) bonus in severance base; full target bonus for year of termination without proration or performance; extended COBRA or lump-sum benefits payment; outplacement; acceleration of all equity; severance on death/disability matching without-Cause; payment timing that may raise 409A issues; weak or missing release condition; survival of severance even if covenants breached.

Assessment: Market severance for non-CEO senior executives is commonly 1x base (sometimes + target bonus) and 12 months COBRA; CEO often 1.5x–2x base+bonus with 18–24 months. Stacking full equity acceleration on top of rich cash severance is aggressive absent CIC.

Risk: High.

Recommendation: COUNTER to market band.
- Cash: [1.0x–2.0x] base salary only, or base + target bonus only for CEO / critical hire; paid as salary continuation or in installments compliant with 409A (specify separation-from-service and specified-employee delay).
- Bonus: pro-rata based on actual performance for year of termination, paid when bonuses are paid to active executives.
- COBRA: Company-paid portion for severance period (or taxable lump sum equivalent); executive remains responsible for employee portion if continuation structure used.
- Condition 100% of severance (and any acceleration) on: (i) irrevocable release within time limits; (ii) continued compliance with restrictive covenants and return of property; (iii) resignation from all positions/boards.
- Cause / voluntary without Good Reason: accrued obligations only (unpaid base through termination date, unreimbursed expenses, vested benefits).
- Reject severance survival after material covenant breach; include clawback/offset right.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. CHANGE IN CONTROL; EQUITY ACCELERATION
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Company draft: Double-trigger — qualifying termination (without Cause / for Good Reason) within [12–24] months post-CIC triggers severance enhancement and equity acceleration per award agreements. No single-trigger vesting on CIC alone. Definition of CIC aligned with equity plan / 409A.

Counterparty markup: Single-trigger vesting of all unvested equity on CIC; walk-right Good Reason on CIC alone; 280G gross-up; modified cutback vs. full cutback; broader CIC definition (e.g., mere sale of minority stake or Board turnover without loss of control).

Assessment: Single-trigger equity and tax gross-ups are off-market for new agreements at most companies (especially PE-backed and public issuers sensitive to ISS/Glass Lewis). Double-trigger remains dominant market standard. 280G best-net / cutback preferred over gross-up.

Risk: Critical (single-trigger + gross-up).

Recommendation: REJECT single-trigger and gross-up; ACCEPT refined double-trigger.
- Double-trigger window: 12–24 months post-CIC.
- Acceleration: full acceleration of time-based awards on double-trigger; performance awards vest at target or based on actual performance through CIC, per plan — do not default to max.
- 280G: “best-net” cutback (executive receives greater of full pay with excise tax borne by executive, or cutback to safe harbor); no gross-up.
- Align CIC definition with equity plan and Code §409A / §280G regulations; reject hair-trigger Board-change definitions disconnected from voting control.
- If counterparty insists on enhanced CIC cash, trade against single-trigger equity rather than granting both.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. RESTRICTIVE COVENANTS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Company draft: Perpetual confidentiality and IP assignment; non-compete during employment + [12–24] months post-termination; employee and customer non-solicit for same period; non-disparagement mutual or Company-protected; garden leave / notice period optional; reasonableness severability and blue-pencil; covenants acknowledged as consideration for employment and severance.

Counterparty markup: Shortens or deletes non-compete; narrows geographic scope to current counties only; limits customers to those with whom executive had “material direct contact” in last 6–12 months; converts non-solicit to non-hire only; deletes employee non-solicit; makes non-disparagement fully mutual with weak exceptions for legal process; conditions covenants on Company not breaching payment obligations; adds California-style free-standing non-compete waiver even if law of another state governs.

Assessment: Enforceability is jurisdiction-dependent. Overbroad covenants risk total unenforceability; over-narrow covenants fail to protect legitimate goodwill and trade secrets. Tying covenant survival solely to Company payment status creates hold-up leverage.

Risk: High (business protection); Moderate–High (enforceability if overbroad).

Recommendation: COUNTER to balanced, enforceable package.
- Confidentiality / trade secrets: perpetual; Defend Trade Secrets Act notice included.
- IP: present assignment of work product; moral rights waiver where applicable; further-assurances covenant.
- Non-compete: duration [12 months] standard ([18–24] CEO only if supported by consideration and jurisdiction); geography = areas where Company materially does business or executive had responsibility; scope = competing business lines in which executive was materially involved. Consider garden leave as alternative/complement in restrictive jurisdictions.
- Customer non-solicit: customers / prospective customers with whom executive had material contact or about whom executive received confidential information during lookback (12–24 months).
- Employee non-solicit: employees / contractors executive supervised or about whom executive had confidential personnel information; non-solicit not mere non-hire if jurisdiction permits.
- Non-disparagement: mutual, with carve-outs for truthful testimony, legal process, whistleblowing, and protected concerted activity (NLRA).
- Independent consideration: affirm severance and equity eligibility as consideration; do not allow unilateral extinguishment of covenants upon alleged Company payment default — use offset/secure payment mechanics instead.
- Blue-pencil / reformation to maximum enforceable scope; severability.
- Jurisdiction check mandatory before lock: CA (Bus. & Prof. Code §16600 et seq.), CO, MN, other state bans/limits, and any applicable federal developments.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
9. CONFIDENTIALITY, IP, WORK PRODUCT, AND COMPANY PROPERTY
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Company draft: Broad confidential information definition; exclusions for public information and independently developed information; mandatory return of property; present assignment of inventions; exclusion list for pre-existing IP if scheduled.

Counterparty markup: Narrows confidential information; expands exclusions to information “generally known in industry”; requires Company to identify confidential information as such; limits assignment to works created strictly “within scope of duties” during work hours; broad pre-existing IP schedule rights; residual knowledge clause.

Assessment: “Residuals” clauses and narrow assignment language create leakage of Company IP and know-how. Industry-general knowledge exclusions are acceptable if they do not swallow trade secret protection.

Risk: Moderate–High.

Recommendation: ACCEPT WITH REVISION.
- Keep broad confidential information definition tied to non-public Company information, without stamping requirement.
- Standard exclusions: public domain (not via breach), third-party non-confidential receipt, independent development without use of Company confidential information.
- Reject broad residuals licenses that permit use of retained mental impressions of trade secrets.
- IP assignment: all work product created within scope of employment or using Company resources; pre-existing IP scheduled on an exhibit, with limited license to Company if embedded in work product.
- Return-of-property and certification on termination or on request.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
10. CLAWBACK, COMPLIANCE, AND COMPANY POLICIES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Company draft: Executive bound by Company policies (code of conduct, insider trading, clawback, stock ownership, hedging/pledging); compensation subject to clawback under Company policy, exchange rules, and applicable law; no hedging/pledging of Company equity without consent.

Counterparty markup: Limits clawback to restatement-required recovery under SEC/exchange rules only; excludes negotiated severance and time-based equity; requires Company fault or executive misconduct finding; opt-out of future policy changes unless executive consents; deletes hedging restrictions.

Assessment: Public companies must maintain compliant clawback policies (Rule 10D-1). Private companies increasingly adopt contractual clawbacks for fraud, misconduct, and covenant breach. Opt-outs from future policies create administration and governance gaps.

Risk: High (regulatory / governance).

Recommendation: REJECT narrowing that conflicts with law or listing standards; COUNTER elsewhere.
- Clawback applies to: (i) legally mandated recovery; (ii) Company clawback policy as in effect from time to time; (iii) fraud, willful misconduct, or material covenant breach to the extent set forth in agreement or policy.
- Executive acknowledges policies may be amended prospectively and agrees to comply with policies applicable to similarly situated executives.
- Hedging/pledging: prohibit or require pre-clearance consistent with Company policy and investor expectations.
- No contractual commitment that future policy changes require individual consent.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
11. INDEMNIFICATION; D&O INSURANCE; ADVANCEMENT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Company draft: Indemnification to fullest extent permitted by law and consistent with charter/bylaws; advancement subject to undertaking to repay if ultimately not entitled; coverage under D&O program while employed and tail for acts during service; employment agreement does not expand beyond corporate instruments except as expressly stated.

Counterparty markup: Contractual indemnification broader than DGCL/charter (including claims by Company); mandatory advancement within short business-day windows; perpetual tail at specified limits; Company breach if insurer denies; indemnification for executive’s breach of employment agreement or Cause conduct; fee-shifting for enforcement of indemnification rights.

Assessment: Matching charter/bylaws plus D&O is market. Expansion beyond statutory limits, indemnifying Cause conduct, and guaranteed insurer outcomes are not.

Risk: Moderate–High.

Recommendation: ACCEPT WITH REVISION.
- Indemnify and advance to fullest extent permitted by applicable law and governing documents for acts as officer/director/employee.
- Advancement upon undertaking; reasonable process timelines (e.g., 30 days) acceptable.
- Exclude matters where executive is determined to have not met the applicable statutory standard, or proceedings initiated by Company for Cause conduct (subject to final adjudication nuances).
- Maintain D&O coverage no less favorable than that provided to peer officers; six-year tail market for change-in-control or departure in many deals — evaluate cost.
- Employment agreement indemnification supplemental, not duplicative windfall; charter/bylaws control on conflict unless agreement expressly more favorable and legally permitted.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
12. REPRESENTATIONS; CONFLICTS; OTHER AGREEMENTS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Company draft: Executive represents no conflicting agreements; not subject to restrictive covenants that would breach by accepting employment; will not use third-party confidential information; disclosure of prior employer constraints.

Counterparty markup: Qualifies representations by knowledge; deletes prior-employer disclosure; adds Company representation that employment will not violate third-party rights (inappropriate reverse risk shift).

Assessment: Knowledge qualifiers on “no conflicting covenants” are sometimes accepted; Company should still obtain disclosure schedules of prior agreements. Company should not warrant third-party IP/covenant landscapes outside its control.

Risk: Moderate.

Recommendation: ACCEPT WITH REVISION.
- Keep flat representation of no conflicting agreements, or knowledge-qualified with affirmative disclosure schedule of all prior restrictive covenants and pending disputes.
- Executive covenant not to use or disclose third-party confidential information.
- Reject Company representation that hiring does not violate third-party rights beyond Company’s own knowledge of its processes.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
13. DISPUTE RESOLUTION; GOVERNING LAW; REMEDIES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Company draft: Governing law of [Company jurisdiction]; exclusive venue in stated courts or confidential arbitration under designated rules; jury trial waiver if litigation path; prevailing-party fees optional; Company entitled to injunctive relief for restrictive covenant / IP breaches without bond.

Counterparty markup: Executive’s home-state law and venue; mandatory arbitration of all claims including covenant breaches (limiting emergency injunctive relief); loser-pays fee-shifting; deletion of jury waiver; bond requirement for injunctions.

Assessment: Company-favorable governing law/venue is standard when Company is primary drafting party. Arbitration can be acceptable if emergency injunctive relief in court is preserved for covenants/IP/confidentiality. Mandatory loser-pays can chill enforcement.

Risk: Moderate.

Recommendation: COUNTER.
- Governing law: Company headquarters / state of incorporation (confirm non-compete enforceability interaction).
- Forum: arbitration for employment disputes under JAMS/AAA employment rules, confidential, before a single arbitrator — but carve out Company access to courts for temporary restraining orders and preliminary injunctions to enforce restrictive covenants, IP, and confidentiality.
- Each party bears own fees unless statute or bad-faith finding provides otherwise; reject automatic loser-pays.
- Preserve jury waiver if litigation path retained, where enforceable.
- Include DTSA and whistleblower protected-activity carve-outs expressly.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
14. CODE SECTION 409A; TAX; WITHHOLDING
================================================================================

Company draft: 409A savings language; payments intended to be exempt or compliant; specified-employee six-month delay; no Company gross-up for 409A taxes; withholding rights; executive responsible for personal taxes.

Counterparty markup: Company representation of 409A compliance; Company indemnity for 409A taxes/penalties; acceleration rights that break 409A; short-term deferral claims without supporting structure.

Assessment: Company indemnity for 409A is off-market. Savings clauses and administrative cooperation are appropriate.

Risk: High (if indemnity or noncompliant timing accepted).

Recommendation: REJECT 409A gross-up/indemnity; ACCEPT technical savings language.
- Intent to comply; interpret and administer accordingly; permit corrective amendments if possible.
- Specify separation-from-service definitions and payment schedules compatible with exemptions (separation pay, short-term deferral) or compliant fixed schedules.
- No tax gross-ups (409A, 280G, or otherwise).
- Standard withholding and wage-deduction authorizations to the extent permitted by law.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
15. MISCELLANEOUS (AMENDMENT, ASSIGNMENT, ENTIRE AGREEMENT, SURVIVAL)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Company draft: Written amendments signed by both parties; Company may assign to successor; executive may not assign; entire agreement superseding prior arrangements (with stated carve-outs for equity award agreements and indemnification rights); severability; counterparts; survival of covenants, IP, confidentiality, indemnification.

Counterparty markup: Executive consent required for any Company assignment even in CIC; prior offer letters and side emails survive; oral modification possible; survival limited.

Assessment: Assignment to CIC successor without executive consent is essential and market. Entire agreement should cleanly supersede prior compensatory promises except identified equity/indemnity instruments.

Risk: Moderate.

Recommendation: ACCEPT WITH REVISION.
- Company may assign to affiliate or successor in connection with merger, sale, or reorganization without executive consent; successor assumption required for Company’s protection as well.
- Entire agreement + integration; supersede prior employment terms, offer letters, and term sheets, with express exceptions list (equity awards, indemnification under charter/bylaws, confidential invention assignment if separate).
- Amendments only in signed writing; no oral waiver of material terms.
- Clear survival clause.

================================================================================
IV. DEVIATION HEAT MAP (SUMMARY TABLE)
================================================================================

Provision                         | Deviation vs. Company Draft      | Market Fit      | Risk      | Disposition
----------------------------------|----------------------------------|-----------------|-----------|---------------------------
Duties / outside boards           | Broader outside activity         | Near market     | Moderate  | Accept w/ caps & consent
Term / non-renewal = w/o Cause    | Economic expansion               | CEO-only market | High      | Counter (severance model)
Cause definition                  | Heavier willfulness + cure       | Executive-fav.  | Critical  | Reject core dilutions
Good Reason                       | Material expansion + CIC walk    | Off-market wide | Critical  | Counter to narrow set
Base / bonus guarantees           | Floors & deemed earning          | Off-market      | High      | Counter (target only)
Severance multiple & components   | Higher multiple + target bonus   | Upper quartile  | High      | Counter to band
Equity single-trigger             | CIC vesting without termination  | Off-market      | Critical  | Reject
280G gross-up                     | Full gross-up                    | Off-market      | Critical  | Reject (best-net)
Non-compete scope/duration        | Narrow / delete                  | Depends on jdx  | High      | Counter balanced
Clawback narrowing                | Restatement-only                 | Non-compliant*  | High      | Reject
Indemnification expansion         | Beyond law / Cause covered       | Off-market      | Mod-High  | Accept w/ statutory cap
409A / tax indemnity              | Company indemnity                | Off-market      | High      | Reject
Dispute resolution                | Executive forum / loser-pays     | Mixed           | Moderate  | Counter (arb + injunction carve-out)
Assignment / integration          | Consent to assign; soft merger   | Off-market      | Moderate  | Reject consent requirement

*If issuer is subject to Rule 10D-1 / exchange clawback listing standards.

================================================================================
V. NEGOTIATION STRATEGY AND TRADE CALENDAR
================================================================================

1. Open constructively. Acknowledge market-standard executive protections (process on Cause, narrow Good Reason, double-trigger equity, indemnification aligned with charter, outside board cap, 409A savings).

2. Anchor on three non-negotiables.
   (a) Cause and Good Reason definitions that preserve Company performance management and avoid single-trigger walk rights.
   (b) No single-trigger equity acceleration; no 280G/409A gross-up.
   (c) Clawback and policy compliance aligned with law and governance.

3. Value trades (give ↔ get).
   - Give: modestly higher cash severance multiple or longer COBRA ↔ Get: clean double-trigger only; tight Good Reason; full release condition.
   - Give: one pre-approved outside board ↔ Get: strong non-compete / customer non-solicit package.
   - Give: contractual advancement timelines ↔ Get: no expansion of indemnifiable conduct beyond statute/charter.
   - Give: arbitration of employment claims ↔ Get: court injunctive relief carve-out for covenants/IP.

4. Sequencing. Resolve Cause / Good Reason / severance / equity acceleration before fine-tuning covenants and boilerplate; economics drive leverage on protective covenants.

5. Documentation hygiene. Push substantive equity terms into award agreements; keep employment agreement at eligibility + cross-reference level. Run 409A and, if applicable, 280G modeling before signing. Confirm restrictive-covenant enforceability under chosen governing law and primary work state.

6. Release and logistics. Prepare form of release as exhibit; align payment timing with release effectiveness and 409A; collect pre-existing IP schedule and prior-covenant disclosure schedule as signing conditions.

================================================================================
VI. RECOMMENDED MARK-UP POSTURE (PLAYBOOK SHORT FORM)
================================================================================

ACCEPT
- Hearing/process rights before Cause termination (not supermajority).
- Cure period for curable performance/breach prongs.
- Narrow Good Reason (material diminution; material salary cut; material Company breach; qualifying relocation) with notice-and-cure.
- Double-trigger equity framework.
- Mutual non-disparagement with legal-process and protected-activity carve-outs.
- Indemnification and D&O aligned with charter/bylaws and peer coverage.
- 409A savings language; best-net 280G cutback.
- Limited outside board service with consent.

ACCEPT WITH REVISION
- Severance multiple and COBRA duration → bring inside market band; condition on release + covenant compliance.
- Customer/employee non-solicit definitions → material contact / confidential information lookback.
- Arbitration → preserve emergency injunctive relief.
- Bonus language → target opportunity; actual performance; pro-rata on qualifying termination.

COUNTER
- Non-renewal treated as without-Cause full package → reduced or use pure at-will + severance model.
- Expansive Good Reason list → delete non-material and pure-CIC triggers.
- Equity terms hardwired in employment agreement → move to award agreements.
- Weak release conditions → irrevocable release as condition precedent.

REJECT
- Single-trigger equity vesting on CIC.
- 280G or 409A tax gross-up / Company tax indemnity.
- Cure rights for fraud, embezzlement, or criminal conduct.
- Clawback limited in ways that conflict with mandatory recovery rules or core misconduct recovery.
- Executive consent right to Company assignment in CIC.
- Residuals licenses that undermine trade secret protection.
- Severance that survives material breach of restrictive covenants without clawback.

================================================================================
VII. OPEN ITEMS AND INFORMATION NEEDED
================================================================================

1. Final executive title, reporting line, work location(s), and whether role is CEO-level for market banding.
2. Cash compensation terms already agreed in offer/term sheet (base, target bonus %, sign-on).
3. Proposed equity mix (options / RSUs / PSUs), vesting cadence, and plan form acceleration standard.
4. Public vs. private issuer status; any exchange listing or PE sponsor clawback/governance requirements.
5. Controlling state law preference and executive residence / primary work state (non-compete critical path).
6. Existing D&O program limits and whether a six-year tail is commercially available/costed.
7. Any side letters, prior consulting arrangements, or outstanding restrictive covenants from prior employers.
8. 280G exposure if a CIC is reasonably anticipated during the term (clean room modeling).
9. Form of release, arbitration rules selection, and benefit plan summaries to annex or cross-reference.
10. Confirmation whether Board or Comp Committee approval is required pre-execution and timing for that consent.

================================================================================
VIII. CONCLUSION
================================================================================

The counterparty redline is a sophisticated, executive-favorable markup. It does not require a wholesale reset, but it does require disciplined resistance on definitions that control termination economics (Cause / Good Reason), equity acceleration architecture (double-trigger only), tax gross-ups, clawback alignment, and enforceable protective covenants. A balanced counter that accepts process fairness and market severance while rejecting structural giveaways should be defensible against peer-company practice and firm precedent.

We recommend circulating a responsive redline implementing the dispositions in Sections III–VI, together with a short issues list for business principals highlighting the Critical and High items only. Counsel should complete jurisdiction-specific covenant enforceability and 409A/280G checks before the agreement is finalized.

Please advise if you would like: (a) a responsive redline markup; (b) alternate CEO-tier vs. non-CEO tier fallback packages; or (c) a board/comp-committee summary slide version of this memorandum.
